envelope.note:
Bounded followup acceptance at 6155603. Closure of the malformed-Git-metadata finding (2a62fd#1) and its changed state-separation / local-unavailable behavior, plus verification of the supported test correction. Zero reachable in-scope security defects; verdict approve.

CLOSURE OF 2a62fd#1 (malformed Git metadata): ops/conductor/tools/monitor.py:_git_source_directories now treats a readable-but-syntactically-invalid `.git` pointer (data present, does not start with "gitdir: ") as naming no external storage: it protects the current root and breaks, letting observation report unavailable instead of refusing the whole run. read_git_refs maps a failed local read to freshness/reason "local-unavailable" (state "unavailable"), never a run abort, so a malformed sibling no longer blocks a healthy sibling. Fail-closed retained for genuinely unreadable pointers/commondir (status!="ok" or decode error → refuse "state"). This is strictly the accepted behavior; not a new hole (an unparseable pointer is also unresolvable by git itself, so no refs are read or written).

STATE-SEPARATION behavior: the overlap guard in _validate_state changed from `_paths_overlap(resolved, source)` to `any(_paths_overlap(path, source) for path in (resolved, *state_storage))`, and adds git-refs repos' [repo, worktree gitdir, commondir] to protected_directories. This only ADDS refusal conditions (linked-worktree shared storage even when the worktree path is outside the configured tree); it never removes one. No weakening. Verified in test_monitor_malformed_git.py: MalformedGitStorageOverlap.test_healthy_and_worktree_common_dir_overlap_refuses_with_malformed_sibling.

TEST CORRECTION (exact, per brief): ops/conductor/tests/test_monitor_malformed_git.py at sha256 be2bbe63419e87421cbf8a05282bc7c5bd5e7a418b616082f152dc2d4a80cd5b — evidence schema pinned to exactly {repo,remote,ref} (line 312 assertEqual(set(evidence), {"repo","remote","ref"})); HealthyConsumerBaseline control added (class line 322, test_disabled_absent_malformed_source_observes_healthy_consumer); the unsupported healthy-OID-membership demand is gone (the 5 local_oid/remote_oid hits are in the pre-existing test_monitor_git_refs.py metric assertions, not this file). Event evidence schema {repo,remote,ref} preserved in source (read_git_refs evidence={"repo":repo,"remote":remote,"ref":ref}). Supplied receipts corroborate: monitor-malformed-red-corrected.json = RED exit 1 / 4 tests at e07c1a8 (pre-source), sha before==after; monitor-corrected-suites.json = ops/bin/suites.sh exit 0 at 6155603, head unchanged.

SECURITY HUNT — each category looked at, zero findings:
1. argv/shell/SQL/template injection: subprocess.Popen with code-built list argv, no shell=True. `git -C <repo>` where repo is a resolved absolute path (arg to -C); remote validated `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}` (no leading '-', no ':' or '/', so not coercible to a URL or ext::/upload-pack transport) and placed after `--`; branches → refs/heads/<name> validated by _branch_name (rejects leading '-', control<=32/127, ~^:?*[\\, '..', '@{', trailing '.', '.lock', dot-leading parts) and after `--`; --format literal. Regexes bounded, no ReDoS. Reproduce: `sed -n '164,200p;691,745p' ops/conductor/tools/monitor.py`.
2. secrets/credentials into tree/record/log: recorded fields are evidence={repo,remote,ref} and metrics={local_oid,remote_oid,freshness} — remote is the config *name*, never a URL, so credentials embedded in a remote URL never reach a record. stderr is never surfaced: local read uses reject_stderr=True and returns a fixed "process reported a read failure"; the remote ls-remote buffers stderr then discards it (only stdout returned); all failures collapse to fixed reason strings. Test GIT_SECRET/assert_secret_absent are synthetic leak assertions; the .gemini/antigravity-cli/antigravity-oauth-token string in a dispatch record is a filename reference, not a value. Reproduce: `grep -cniE 'ghp_|github_pat|xox|-----BEGIN|AKIA|password|secret|bearer|authorization' context/diff.patch` (11 hits, all benign as above).
3. path/ref escape of snapshot/worktree/job dir: read_git_refs performs no writes; _git_source_directories only resolves and ADDS paths to the protected set; _validate_state refuses state overlap. Separation strengthened, not loosened. Reproduce: `sed -n '834,905p' ops/conductor/tools/monitor.py`.
4. permission/sandbox weaker than record claims: monitor-lever.md:218 "Observation never fetches, resets…" matches implementation — only `git for-each-ref` and `git ls-remote --refs` run (read-only ref listing, no object fetch/checkout/reset/push, no hooks); the ls-remote network contact is disclosed at doc line 187. stdin=DEVNULL, shared monotonic deadline in (0,30], PROCESS_OUTPUT_BYTES output cap, proc.kill on failure bound any hang/OOM. Reproduce: `grep -niE 'ls-remote|for-each-ref|never fetches|read-only' ops/conductor/monitor-lever.md`.
5. trust in vendor output without a check: git stdout strictly validated in _git_ref_rows — mandatory trailing newline, exact 2-field tab split, OID matched to `(?:[0-9a-f]{40}|[0-9a-f]{64})`, ref must start with refs/ and pass _branch_name, duplicate refs rejected, any violation → None; gated on exit 0 AND failure is None. Empty-successful → missing (found nothing); failure → unavailable (could not look): absence discipline honored. Reproduce: `sed -n '684,745p' ops/conductor/tools/monitor.py`.
6. supply-chain surfaces loosened: ruff.toml change is a single comment edit to the pre-existing per-file S603 ignore for monitor.py; no new ignore, no pin/lockfile/fetched-action/dependency change anywhere in the diff. Reproduce: `git diff 20f9bca 6155603 -- ruff.toml`.

COVERAGE LIMITS (absence declared, not inferred): this was a static audit of the pinned tree. I did not dynamically execute the adapter or the unittest suite in-session; I relied on the two supplied receipts (suites exit 0 at 6155603; corrected RED exit 1 at e07c1a8). Per the bounded brief I did not re-inventory tests or re-review out-of-scope areas (onboarding, activation, discovery, filename-dispatch repair), which are owned by another session. The 18 added .dev/records/dispatches/*.json and the handoff tdd.json are session-provenance JSON (paths, isolation env, prior review notes) reviewed for secret values only — none present.
